Finally, a Rolls-Royce Ghost That Doesn’t Cost an Arm and a Leg!
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc
While some say the Rolls-Royce Ghost is the best full-size luxury sedan out there, others would opt for a Mercedes-Maybach S-Class or a Bentley Flying Spur, arguing that these are better.
And we think that you believe in the former model. After all, here you are, looking to find out more details about the car pictured above, including the model year, mileage, and how much it costs, among other things, because this one is for sale in the United States of America, and won’t affect your finances badly enough that the missus won’t talk to you anymore.
To the average Joe, this Rolls-Royce Ghost looks modern, but real petrolheads know that they are looking at the previous generation . This model was assembled from 2009 to 2020, and it is based on the same platform as the F10 BMW 5 Series, the F01 7 Series, and its two-door grand touring siblings, namely the Wraith and the Dawn.
This model measured up to 219.3 inches (5,569 mm) from bumper to bumper in the EWB (extended wheelbase) configuration, and was 212.6 inches (5,399 mm) long in the regular variant. The space between the axles measured 136.4 inches (3,465 mm) in the former, and 129.7 inches (3,295 mm) in the latter.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc A V12 engine (what else?) breathes air from behind that imposing grille, and it is a 6.6-liter mill in this case, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission, and rear-wheel drive. The twin-turbocharged V12 was rated at 562 hp (419 kW/570 ps) and 575 pound-feet (780 Nm) of torque when the car rolled off the line, enabling 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in less than five seconds, and a top speed electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph).
This pictured Rolls-Royce Ghost is a 2015 model year car. It features a blue look on the outside, and it is unknown whether it’s a paint finish or a wrap, as the vendor hasn’t mentioned it. There are no chrome details anymore, as everything was blacked out. The wheels are also black, and so its the interior, with its high-end leather upholstery, wood trim, traditional buttons and knobs, and an overall design that hasn’t aged badly at all.
We found this previous-generation British luxury sedan on Instagram, where it was advertised by @imad_mcc. The vendor said that the odometer read 28,836 miles (46,407 km) at the time of cataloging, so you are looking at a low-mileage machine. The dealer accepts trades, offers financing, and shipping nationwide is possible, albeit at an extra cost.
Speaking of the cost, how much do you think this 2015 Rolls-Royce Ghost is? That wold be $109,995, and that’s new Mercedes- AMG E 53 E-Class territory. Is this luxury sedan worth the asking price in your opinion? I think it does, and if you want to buy it, don’t forget that the high maintenance could easily bankrupt you.
